#!/usr/bin/env python3 """CSEF code-of-conduct comparison. Compares a code of conduct (an industry code, a company code, a draft code under the EU KIDS Act) with: 1. the structural expectations for codes of conduct in the EU KIDS Act proposal (Art. 17, Art. 23, Recital 39); 2. the CSEF rules in scope (profiles, age bands, level, packs). For each rule it reports: covered, partial (topic mentioned, or only weak commitment), missing, or possible conflict (the code permits something the rule forbids). This is a first pass based on wording; every result needs a person (or the csef-review skill) to confirm meaning. python3 tooling/coc.py --input code.pdf [--name "Example Code"] [--level 1|2|3] [--profiles A,C] [--bands B2,B3] [--pack file.yaml] [--out-dir csef-coc] [--formats md,html,json] Input: .txt, .md, .html, .pdf (pdftotext or pypdf) or .docx (python-docx). Licence: Apache-2.0 """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime as dt import html as htmllib import json import re import shutil import subprocess import sys import unicodedata from pathlib import Path import yaml sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)) import scan # noqa: E402 TOOL = "csef-coc" STRONG = r"\b(must|shall|will|never|do not|does not|are not|is not|may not|cannot|can not|prohibit\w*|ban(s|ned)?|required?|commit\w*|ensure\w*|undertake\w*|guarantee\w*|not permitted|not allowed)\b" WEAK = r"\b(should|encourag\w*|endeavou?r\w*|aim(s)? to|where possible|where appropriate|where feasible|strive\w*|consider\w*|recommend\w*|seek to|best efforts|as far as possible|voluntar\w*)\b" PERMISSIVE = r"\b(may|can|could|is permitted|are permitted|permitted|allowed|acceptable|optional|at (their|its) discretion|provided that|as long as|subject to|is possible)\b" NEGATION = r"\b(not|never|no|nor|prohibit\w*|ban(s|ned)?|avoid\w*|without|refrain\w*|cannot|must not|may not|shall not|exclude\w*|forbid\w*)\b" STATUS_ORDER = ["conflict", "missing", "partial", "covered", "not_applicable"] STATUS_LABEL = {"conflict": "Possible conflict", "missing": "Missing", "partial": "Partial", "covered": "Covered", "not_applicable": "Not expected in a code"} STATUS_SEV = {"conflict": "BLOCK", "missing": "REVIEW", "partial": "WARN", "covered": "OK", "not_applicable": "NEXT"} # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- text def norm(s: str) -> str: s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", s) s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower() s = s.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'") s = re.sub(r"[-_/]", " ", s) return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip() def read_input(path: Path) -> str: suf = path.suffix.lower() if suf in (".txt", ".md", ".markdown"): return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") if suf in (".html", ".htm"): t = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") t = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style).*?", " ", t) t = re.sub(r"(?i)|", "\n", t) return htmllib.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", t)) if suf == ".pdf": if shutil.which("pdftotext"): r = subprocess.run(["pdftotext", "-layout", str(path), "-"], capture_output=True, text=True) if r.returncode == 0: return r.stdout try: from pypdf import PdfReader # type: ignore return "\n".join(p.extract_text() or "" for p in PdfReader(str(path)).pages) except ImportError: raise RuntimeError("Reading PDF needs pdftotext (poppler) or `pip install pypdf`.") if suf == ".docx": try: from docx import Document # type: ignore except ImportError: raise RuntimeError("Reading .docx needs `pip install python-docx`.") d = Document(str(path)) parts = [p.text for p in d.paragraphs] for t in d.tables: for row in t.rows: parts.append(" | ".join(c.text for c in row.cells)) return "\n".join(parts) raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported input type: {suf} (use .txt, .md, .html, .pdf or .docx)") def clauses(text: str): """Split into clauses: paragraphs and list items, keeping the nearest heading.""" out, heading, buf = [], "", [] def flush(): if buf: t = " ".join(x.strip() for x in buf).strip() if len(t) > 15: out.append({"id": f"C{len(out) + 1}", "heading": heading, "text": t}) buf.clear() for raw in text.splitlines(): line = raw.strip() if not line: flush() continue if re.match(r"^(#{1,6}\s|article\s+\d+|section\s+\d+|part\s+[ivx\d]+|chapter\s+\d+)", line, re.I) or ( len(line) < 80 and line.isupper() and len(line.split()) <= 10): len(groups), "clauses": best[2]} def strength(text_n: str) -> str: if re.search(STRONG, text_n): return "strong" if re.search(WEAK, text_n): return "weak" return "neutral" def find_conflicts(topic, and not re.search(NEGATION, s): hit = s if hit: out.append({"clause": c["id"], "heading": c["heading"], "sentence": hit}) break return out[:3] def assess(groups, cls, need=None, topic=None): m = # Child-Safe EdTech Framework (CSEF): rule catalogue. Single source of truth.
# Generated documents (catalogue, checklists, skill references, semgrep rules)
# are built from this file by tooling/build.py. Do not edit those by hand.
#
# Field reference (see framework/00-introduction.md for the full explanation):
#   id          PREFIX-AREA-NN. Prefixes: CORE, A (educational games), B (game-based
#               applications), C (gamified applications), AGE (age-band modifiers).
#   level       MUST | SHOULD
#   tier        1 = legal baseline, 2 = forward-compliant, 3 = best practice
#   profiles    [core] applies to every product; otherwise any of [A, B, C]
#   age_bands   [all] or any of [B1, B2, B3, B4, B5]
#   features    optional. Rule only applies if the product declares one of these
#               features in its manifest (or if there is no manifest).
#   sources     ids from framework/sources.yaml or a loaded pack
#   effort      low | medium | high (used to prioritise the improvement list)
#   detection   method: static | manifest | manual | mixed, plus patterns

version: "0.14.0"

# Rules merged into others. Packs, waivers and csef-ignore comments that use an old id keep working:
# the tools map it to the rule that replaced it.
retired:
  - {id: A-SOC-01, replaced_by: CORE-SAF-05, since: "0.11.0"}
  - {id: A-ECO-04, replaced_by: A-MOT-01, since: "0.11.0"}
  - {id: CORE-SAF-11, replaced_by: CORE-CHT-08, since: "0.11.0"}

rules:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: governance
  - id: CORE-GOV-01
    title: Product declares its CSEF manifest
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The repository contains a CSEF manifest (csef.yaml) declaring profiles, age bands,
      context of use, GDPR role, features, AI use, third parties and chosen compliance level.
    rationale: >
      Accountability (GDPR Art. 5(2)) requires being able to show what the product does with
      children's data. The manifest is also what lets the checks select the right rules.
    improvement: Copy templates/csef.yaml to the repository root and fill it in with the product owner.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: manifest_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-GOV-02
    title: Legal scope of the EU KIDS Act is assessed and recorded
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The manifest records whether the product is in scope of the EU KIDS Act (online game,
      AI companion, general conversational chatbot, social or video-sharing service) or exempt
      as a service designed primarily for education and operated by or on behalf of an
      educational establishment (Art. 2(4)(c)).
    rationale: >
      The same product can be exempt when deployed by a school and in scope when offered
      directly to families. Teams must know which situation they are in for each channel.
    improvement: Fill the `legal_scope.kids_act` field in csef.yaml for each distribution channel.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-FAQ]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: kids_act_scope_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-GOV-03
    title: Child rights impact assessment
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A child rights impact assessment (or a risk review in the sense of the DSA Art. 28
      guidelines) is documented, considers the best interests of the child, and involves
      children, guardians and educators in testing.
    rationale: >
      The DSA guidelines and UN General Comment No. 25 ask providers to weigh all children's
      rights (protection, participation, provision), not only data protection.
    improvement: Extend the DPIA with a child rights section (templates/dpia-starter.md, part C).
    effort: medium
    sources: [DSA-G28, UNCRC-GC25, EUKO]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: data protection
  - id: CORE-DAT-01
    title: DPIA before launch
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A Data Protection Impact Assessment exists before launch when children's data is processed
      at scale, with new technology (including AI), or for systematic monitoring of learners.
    rationale: Processing of vulnerable data subjects with new technology is high risk under GDPR Art. 35.
    improvement: >
      Start a DPIA with templates/dpia-starter.md. If the school or Ministry is controller, provide
      them the technical input; they sign it.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: dpia_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-02
    title: Controller and processor roles are defined, with processor agreements
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The manifest states whether the provider acts as controller or processor, and every third
      party that touches personal data has a data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28).
    rationale: Without defined roles nobody is accountable for legal basis, DPIA or data subject requests.
    improvement: "Record `gdpr_role` and `dpa_signed: true` for each third party, or remove the integration."
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: third_party_without_dpa, confidence: high}
        - {type: manifest, check: gdpr_role_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-03
    title: No transfers outside the EEA without a valid mechanism
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Personal data of minors is hosted in the EEA, or every transfer outside it has a documented
      transfer mechanism (adequacy decision, SCCs plus transfer impact assessment).
    rationale: GDPR Chapter V.
    improvement: Move hosting to an EEA region or record `transfer_mechanism` for the third party.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: transfer_outside_eea, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-04
    title: No personal data in analytics events
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Analytics and telemetry events carry no direct identifiers (name, email, phone, IP address,
      precise location, free text typed by the child). Use pseudonymous IDs.
    rationale: Data minimisation and purpose limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(c)).
    improvement: Replace identifiers with a pseudonymous learner ID and drop free-text fields from events.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          pattern: '(track|logEvent|capture|analytics\.\w+)\s*\([^)]*\b(email|e_mail|full_?name|first_?name|last_?name|phone|ip_?address|latitude|longitude)\b'
          flags: i

  - id: CORE-DAT-05
    title: Retention periods enforced by code
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Each category of learner data has a retention period, enforced by an automated deletion
      or anonymisation job, not only by policy text.
    rationale: Storage limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)).
    improvement: Add a scheduled deletion job per data category and list it in csef.yaml `retention`.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: retention_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-DAT-06
    title: Data subject rights are supported by tooling
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Access, rectification, erasure and export of a learner's data can be executed by tooling
      (admin function or script), and the process is tested.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 15 to 20. Schools as controllers depend on the processor to execute requests.
    improvement: Build an admin export and delete function per learner and test it each release.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DAT-07
    title: No real learner data outside production
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Seeds, fixtures, tests, staging databases and prompts sent to development AI tools use
      synthetic data only.
    rationale: Purpose limitation and security (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(f), Art. 32).
    improvement: Use a synthetic data generator (e.g. Faker) and block production dumps in non-production environments.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          globs: ['*seed*', '*fixture*', '*mock*', '*.sql', '*test*']
          pattern: '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(gmail|hotmail|outlook|yahoo|sapo|live|icloud)\.(com|pt|es|fr|de)'
          flags: i

  - id: CORE-DAT-08
    title: No biometric identification of minors
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: The product does not process face, voice or fingerprint data to identify children.
    rationale: Biometric data for identification is special category data (GDPR Art. 9). Disproportionate in education.
    improvement: Remove face or voice recognition. Use class codes, picture passwords or teacher-managed login.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: high, names: [face-api.js, '@vladmandic/face-api', face_recognition, deepface, '@aws-sdk/client-rekognition', amazon-rekognition, azure-cognitiveservices-face, '@azure/cognitiveservices-face']}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(faceRecognition|recognizeFace|FaceMatcher|detectAllFaces|compareFaces|voiceprint|speakerRecognition)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-09
    title: Geolocation off and not collected unless essential
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Precise geolocation is not collected. If a feature truly needs it, it is off by default
      and turned off again at the end of the session.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(a) and 11(2) (applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b)). DSA Art. 28 guidelines on safe defaults.
    improvement: Remove location permissions or gate them behind an explicit, session-limited opt-in.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(navigator\.geolocation|getCurrentPosition|watchPosition|ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION|NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription|CLLocationManager|Input\.location\.Start)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-10
    title: Microphone and camera off by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Access to microphone and camera is off by default, requested only at the moment of use
      for a clear learning purpose, and the recording is not kept longer than needed.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(b), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b).
    improvement: Request media permissions just-in-time with a child-friendly explanation; never at start-up.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(getUserMedia|RECORD_AUDIO|android\.permission\.CAMERA|NSMicrophoneUsageDescription|NSCameraUsageDescription|Microphone\.Start|WebCamTexture)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-11
    title: Consent for non-essential storage and cookies
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Non-essential cookies and local storage are only set after valid consent. Where consent is the legal
      basis for a child below the national age of digital consent, the guardian gives it (see AGE-B4-01).
    rationale: ePrivacy Art. 5(3). The national consent age (GDPR Art. 8) is set out in AGE-B4-01.
    improvement: Keep only strictly necessary storage, or add a guardian-facing consent flow.
    effort: medium
    sources: [EPRIV, GDPR, EDPB-CONSENT]
    detection:
      method: manual


  - id: CORE-DAT-12
    title: Child-friendly privacy information
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Privacy information exists in a version the target age can understand (very short sentences,
      icons, audio for non-readers), plus a full version for adults.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 12(1) requires clear language, in particular for information addressed to a child.
    improvement: Write a one-screen child version of the privacy notice and test it with children of the target age.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manual


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: personal questions (feature: survey)
  # Questions to the child or family about the child's life, family, opinions, interests or feelings:
  # surveys, "about me" profiles, mood check-ins, onboarding questions. Quizzes about learning content are
  # assessment, not survey. Template for the register: templates/survey-register.md.
  - id: CORE-DAT-13
    title: Every personal question has a recorded purpose and can be skipped
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey]
    requirement: >
      Each question asked to a child or guardian about the child's life, family, opinions, interests
      or feelings is listed in a survey register with its learning purpose, the closed answers, who
      answers it, who can see the answers, how long they are kept and the legal basis. Every question
      offers "prefer not to say" with the same weight as the other answers, the whole set can be
      skipped, no part of the product depends on answering, and answering earns no points, coins,
      badges or other rewards.
    rationale: >
      Purpose limitation and data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(c)) and data protection by design
      (Art. 25). A question without a purpose is data collected "just in case". Forcing, nudging or
      rewarding answers are deceptive design patterns (EDPB Guidelines 03/2022: skipping, stirring,
      obstructing), and a reward for telling turns disclosure into a game.
    improvement: Write the register from templates/survey-register.md, delete every question without a purpose, add "prefer not to say" and remove rewards for answering.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, EDPB-DDP, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_register_missing, confidence: high}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '((answer|complete|fill in|finish) (the |this |our )?(survey|questions?|questionnaire|about me)\W.{0,40}(earn|get|win|receive|unlock)\W.{0,20}(coins?|points?|gems?|xp|badges?|stars?)|(responde|completa|preenche|termina) (ao |o |a )?(inqu[eé]rito|question[aá]rio|perguntas?)\W.{0,40}(ganha|recebe|desbloqueia)\W.{0,20}(moedas|pontos|gemas|medalhas?|estrelas))'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-14
    title: No personal data about other people is collected from children
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey, ugc, chat, ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      The product does not ask children for the names, photos, voices, ages, jobs, health,
      whereabouts or contact details of relatives, friends or other people, and AI characters do
      not ask for them either. Where an activity needs such people, the child uses fictional
      characters or a generic role ("a grandparent"), and creation tools offer avatars instead of
      photos of real people.
    rationale: >
      The other person is not informed and cannot exercise their rights (GDPR Art. 14), there is
      rarely a legal basis (Art. 6), and children cannot judge what is safe to tell about others.
      Details about relatives can also reveal special category data (see CORE-DAT-15).
    improvement: Replace name and detail fields about other people with fictional characters picked from a list, and tell AI prompts not to ask about real people.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '((mum|mom|mother|dad|father|grand(ma|pa|mother|father)|brother|sister|best friend)''?s? (full )?(name|job|age|phone|address|school)\b)'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '((nome|idade|profiss[aã]o|trabalho|telefone|morada|escola) d[oa]s? (teu|tua|teus|tuas) (pai|m[aã]e|av[oóô]s?|irm[aã]os?|irm[aã]s?|tio|tia|primo|prima|amig[oa]s?|melhor amig[oa]))'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-15
    title: No questions that reveal special category data or family vulnerability
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey, ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Children and guardians are not asked, directly or indirectly, about racial or ethnic origin,
      religion or beliefs, health or disability (of the child or of relatives), sexual orientation or
      political opinions, nor about family vulnerability: migration or residence status, parents'
      separation, bereavement, foster or residential care, income, debts or parents' jobs. Support
      needs are asked as product settings (bigger text, read-aloud, support language) chosen by the
      guardian or the child, never as a diagnosis or an origin. Mood check-ins are allowed only when
      the child picks the answer, it is not kept as a history per child (unless the child keeps it for
      themselves), it never becomes a label, and it is never inferred by AI (CORE-AI-01).
    rationale: >
      Data that reveal a special category indirectly, by deduction or cross-referencing, fall under
      GDPR Art. 9 (CJEU C-184/20): an innocent family question can reveal religion, origin or health.
      Vulnerability data is not Art. 9 but is high risk: it can hurt the child, expose them to peers
      and adults, and calls for a DPIA (Art. 35). UN General Comment 25 protects children's privacy,
      including towards the adults around them.
    improvement: Remove these questions, turn diagnoses into settings, and keep low-risk closed questions or move the activity to fiction. If a question is truly needed, the controller (usually the school) decides it with a DPIA and an Art. 9(2) exception.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, CJEU-ART9, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(what is your (religion|ethnicity|nationality)|are you (christian|muslim|jewish|catholic|hindu)|where (are|were) your parents (from|born)|are your parents (separated|divorced)|do you live with (your )?(mum|mom|dad|both)|how much do your parents earn|what (does|do) your (mum|mom|dad|parents) do for (a )?(living|work))'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(qual (é|e) a tua (religi[aã]o|etnia|nacionalidade)|de onde s[aã]o os teus pais|onde nasceram os teus pais|os teus pais (est[aã]o|s[aã]o) (separados|divorciados)|vives com (a tua m[aã]e|o teu pai|os dois)|quanto ganham os teus pais|em que trabalh(a|am) (o teu pai|a tua m[aã]e|os teus pais))'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-16
    title: Who answers personal questions fits the child's age
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey]
    requirement: >
      For ages 3 to 9 (B1, B2), questions about the child's life are answered by a guardian with the
      child, not by the child alone. From 10, the child answers for themselves and guardians are told
      what is asked. From 13 (B4, B5), the child's answers about their opinions and feelings are not
      shown to guardians or teachers by default, unless the child chooses to share them or there is a
      safeguarding concern (CORE-CHT-08).
    rationale: >
      Children's evolving capacities and their right to privacy, including towards parents (UN General
      Comment 25). Guardian tools in the EU KIDS Act proposal (Art. 20) must respect the child's
      privacy. Young children cannot yet weigh what they share; teenagers need a private space.
    improvement: Move questions for under-10s to the guardian page; for teenagers, keep answers private by default and say so.
    effort: medium
    sources: [UNCRC-GC25, KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_answered_by_child, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-DAT-17
    title: Teachers see answers about children's lives only as class totals
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey]
    requirement: >
      Teachers and schools see answers to personal questions only as totals for a group of at least
      5 children per figure. A figure is hidden when it would still reveal a child: when every child
      gave the same answer, when two views differ by one child, or when filters narrow the group.
      Answers are never shown per child, on shared or projected screens, or in rankings. A per-child
      view exists only where the register's purpose requires it (for example, a child asks for help)
      and the child knows.
    rationale: >
      Aggregation over small or uniform groups still identifies people (Article 29 Working Party
      Opinion 05/2014). Minimisation and data protection by default (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 25(2)).
      Knowing a child's private life changes how adults and peers treat them. Extends B-OPS-01 to
      personal questions.
    improvement: Show only totals with a minimum group size, hide uniform or small cells, and remove per-child exports.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, WP216, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_teacher_view_individual, confidence: high}
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_min_group_low, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-18
    title: Answers stay with their purpose and under the family's control
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey]
    requirement: >
      Answers are used only for the purpose in the register. They stay within the school's
      deployment and follow its instructions, are deleted at the end of the retention period, and are
      not used for advertising, profiling beyond the declared personalisation, AI training, or
      research unless B-DAT-01 is met and the approval is recorded. Personalisation based on the
      answers is explained to the child, shown to the guardian for children under 13, and can be
      changed or switched off. The child or guardian can see, correct and delete the answers at any
      time.
    rationale: >
      Purpose limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)), rights of access, rectification and erasure (Art. 15 to
      17), processor duties (Art. 28). Recital 71: decisions based on profiling should not concern a
      child. The EU KIDS Act proposal asks for high privacy by default for minors.
    improvement: Keep answers in the class instance, add see, correct and delete for answers, and make personalisation visible and reversible.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_research_without_approval, confidence: medium}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: learning data (v0.14)
  # Event data, research use and open evidence. See framework/08-learning-data.md and framework/data/.

  - id: CORE-DAT-19
    title: Every logged event is declared in an event catalogue
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product keeps an event catalogue (templates/event-catalogue.yaml) listing every gameplay or usage
      event it logs, each field of each event with its type, and the purpose it serves (operation,
      improvement, evaluation or research). Events and fields that are not in the catalogue are not sent.
      csef.yaml says whether the product logs events (`data_collection`) and links the catalogue.
    rationale: >
      Purpose limitation and data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(c)) and records of processing (Art. 30)
      need to know what is collected and why. Open Game Data's design goal "capture then analyze" is useful
      for research but collects more than a stated purpose needs; a catalogue turns it into "declare, then
      capture". The catalogue is also the allow-list that tooling/evidence.py checks event files against.
    improvement: Copy templates/event-catalogue.yaml, list every event with its fields and purpose, link it from csef.yaml, and remove logging calls that are not in it.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, R-OGD2024]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: event_catalogue_missing, confidence: medium}
        - {type: repo, check: undeclared_event, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-DAT-20
    title: Player codes are random, scoped to one product and not derived from identifiers
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Event data uses a random player code made by the game or the server. It is never a hash or encoding
      of an email, name, username, account id or student number. A code is used in one product only and
      renewed each school year. Codes are not linked across products or providers, except inside a study
      with a recorded approval. The key between codes and accounts stays with the controller.
    rationale: >
      A hash of a known value can be reversed by hashing likely values, so it is not effective
      pseudonymisation (GDPR Art. 4(5), EDPB Guidelines 01/2025). Codes shared across products enable
      profiling of children (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), Recital 38). Keeping the key with the controller lets
      recipients receive data they cannot re-identify (CJEU, EDPS v SRB).
    improvement: Generate player codes with a secure random generator, store the link to accounts in a separate table, rotate codes each school year, and set cross_product_linking to false.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, EDPB-PSEUDO, CJEU-SRB]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          pattern: '((sha1|sha256|sha512|md5|hashlib\.\w+|digest|hmac|btoa|base64\w*|Hash128\.Compute|ComputeHash)\s*\(|createHash\([^)]*\)\s*\.update\s*\()[^;\n]{0,80}\b(e_?mail|user_?name|full_?name|first_?name|last_?name|account_?id|student_?(id|number)|user\.id|userId)\b'
          flags: i
        - {type: manifest, check: player_code_scope, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-21
    title: No fingerprinting attributes in telemetry
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Analytics and gameplay events do not carry device attributes that can single out a device: user agent
      strings, screen size or pixel ratio, installed fonts or plugins, hardware details, advertising ids
      (IDFA, GAID) or unique device ids. One coarse device class (tablet, laptop, desktop, phone, other) per
      session is enough for research and for teachers.
    rationale: >
      Reading such attributes from the device to recognise it is access to terminal equipment under
      ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and needs consent unless strictly necessary (EDPB Guidelines 2/2023). Combined,
      they work as an identifier (GDPR Recital 30).
    improvement: Replace device attributes with one device class computed on the device, and remove advertising and unique device ids from events.
    effort: low
    sources: [EPRIV, EDPB-ART53, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          pattern: '\b(track|logEvent|log_event|trackEvent|capture|sendEvent|analytics\.\w+|Log)\s*\([^;\n]{0,200}(navigator\.userAgent|userAgent|screen\.(width|height|availWidth|availHeight)|devicePixelRatio|hardwareConcurrency|deviceMemory|deviceUniqueIdentifier|advertisingId|idfa|gaid)'
          flags: i
        - type: regex
          confidence: high
          pattern: '\b(AdvertisingIdClient|getAdvertisingIdInfo|ASIdentifierManager|advertisingIdentifier|SystemInfo\.deviceUniqueIdentifier|Settings\.Secure\.ANDROID_ID)\b'

  - id: CORE-DAT-22
    title: Inferences about a child stay at population level by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Detectors that infer a state (stuck, frustrated, idle, likely to quit, ability) are used to improve the
      design for everyone, at population level. They are not shown as labels on a named child, used to rank
      children or used to decide for them, unless the product declares assessment and meets the assessment
      rules (A-ASM-01, B-EVL-01 to 04), and a teacher can see why and override. Emotion is never inferred
      from camera, voice or face.
    rationale: >
      Inferences about a person are personal data. Labels on children invite surveillance and automated
      decisions (GDPR Art. 22, Recital 71); systems that evaluate learners are high-risk (AI Act Annex III)
      and emotion recognition in education is banned (AI Act Art. 5(1)(f)). The EU KIDS Act proposal and UN
      General Comment 25 ask for the child's best interests and privacy by default.
    improvement: Keep detector output in population features; if teachers need it, show class totals, or declare assessment and follow its rules.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA, KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: detectors_teacher_view_without_assessment, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-23
    title: No engagement targets for children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Retention, daily or monthly active users, streak length, sessions per week or growth in playing time
      are not product targets, experiment goals or quality signals for children. Teams report learning,
      completion, help needed, accessibility and natural stopping points instead. Typical time to finish a
      unit may be measured to help teachers plan, never as a number to increase.
    rationale: >
      The EU KIDS Act proposal bans design that leads to excessive use, and the Digital Fairness Act
      proposal targets features that keep minors engaged. Optimising for engagement pulls design towards
      those features. Engagement-based rewards lower intrinsic motivation and learning (Deci et al. 1999;
      Hanus and Fox 2015).
    improvement: Replace engagement KPIs in dashboards, experiments and OKRs with the csef-evidence-0.1 features.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, R-DECI1999, R-HANUS2015]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          pattern: '\b(d1|d7|d30|day_?1|day_?7|day_?30)_?retention\b|\bretention_?(rate|target|goal|kpi)\b|\b(dau|mau|wau)\b|\bstickiness\b|\bstreak_?length_?(goal|target)\b|\bsession_?(length|time)_?(goal|target|kpi)\b'
          flags: i

  - id: CORE-DAT-24
    title: Open releases of learning data hold group figures only
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Data published openly (to a public site, repository or catalogue) holds population features only, in
      the csef-evidence-0.1 format: at least 10 players and 3 classes behind every figure, counts rounded to 5,
      dates to the month, no free text, no per-player, per-class or per-school rows, and no engagement metrics.
      Event-level and player-level data are never published, even with anonymous codes. When the data were
      collected as a processor for schools, the schools' contract allows the release.
    rationale: >
      A stable player code with exact times can single out a child; small groups break aggregation (Article
      29 Working Party, WP216). For the controller holding the key, pseudonymised data stay personal (CJEU,
      EDPS v SRB; EDPB Guidelines 01/2025), so publishing them is a disclosure of personal data. A processor
      may only process on the school's instructions (GDPR Art. 28(3)(a)).
    improvement: Publish with tooling/evidence.py build-feed and check every feed with check-feed before release.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, WP216, CJEU-SRB, EDPB-PSEUDO]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: open_evidence_thresholds, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-25
    title: Research logging runs only in a study build
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Logging for research is off in the normal build. It runs in a study build with its own version branch
      (for example 2.1.0-study), given only to classes that agreed, under a data sharing agreement and an
      ethics approval, with a child-friendly notice and a way to leave the study without leaving the lesson.
      Device storage for research identifiers has a valid basis (consent where ePrivacy Art. 5(3) needs it).
    rationale: >
      Research is a new purpose that needs a compatibility check and safeguards (GDPR Art. 6(4), 89). Storing
      or reading an identifier on the device for a purpose that is not strictly necessary needs consent under
      ePrivacy Art. 5(3) (EDPB Guidelines 2/2023). A separate build keeps the normal product within its
      purpose, and the version branch keeps study data apart (Open Game Data versioning).
    improvement: Add a study build flag that is off by default, record the agreement and approval in csef.yaml, and tag study builds with a version branch.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, EPRIV, EDPB-ART53, R-OGD2024]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: research_logging_default_on, confidence: high}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: commercial
  - id: CORE-COM-01
    title: No advertising or ad tracking SDKs
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No advertising based on profiling of minors and no ad, attribution or fingerprinting SDKs
      in products used by minors.
    rationale: DSA Art. 28(2) bans profiling-based ads to minors on online platforms. The DFA proposal extends this to all traders.
    improvement: Remove the SDK. If marketing attribution is needed, measure it on the adult-facing website only.
    effort: low
    sources: [DSA, DFA, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(Advertisement\.(Initialize|Show|Load)|MobileAds\.Initialize|FB\.Init|AppsFlyer\.initSDK|IronSource\.Agent|LevelPlay\.Init|AdjustConfig)\b'}
        - type: dependency
          confidence: high
          names: [react-native-google-mobile-ads, google-mobile-ads, '@capacitor-community/admob', admob-plus-cordova, react-native-fbsdk, react-native-fbsdk-next, facebook-nodejs-business-sdk, facebook_business, react-native-appsflyer, appsflyer-capacitor-plugin, react-native-adjust, '@adjustcom/adjust-web-sdk', react-native-branch, branch-sdk, '@fingerprintjs/fingerprintjs', '@fingerprintjs/fingerprintjs-pro', Google-Mobile-Ads-SDK, FBSDKCoreKit, AppsFlyerFramework, Adjust, 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads', 'com.facebook.android:facebook-android-sdk', 'com.appsflyer:af-android-sdk', 'com.adjust.sdk:adjust-android', google_mobile_ads, appsflyer_sdk, adjust_sdk, com.unity.ads, com.unity.services.levelplay, com.google.ads.mobile, com.ironsource.sdk, GoogleMobileAds, Unity.Advertisements, Google.Apis.AdSense.v2]
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(googletagservices\.com|doubleclick\.net|connect\.facebook\.net/[^"'' ]*/fbevents\.js|adsbygoogle)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-02
    title: Third-party analytics and session recording reviewed
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Product analytics and session-replay tools are either self-hosted in the EEA or bound by a
      processor agreement that forbids reuse of data. Session recording is not used on child-facing screens.
    rationale: Many analytics vendors reuse data for their own purposes, which would make them controllers (GDPR Art. 28).
    improvement: Prefer self-hosted analytics (e.g. EU-hosted PostHog or Matomo) with IP anonymisation; remove session replay from child screens.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(Firebase\.Analytics|GameAnalyticsSDK|AnalyticsService\.Instance)\b'}
        - type: dependency
          confidence: medium
          names: ['@react-native-firebase/analytics', firebase-analytics, mixpanel-browser, mixpanel-react-native, '@amplitude/analytics-browser', '@segment/analytics-next', '@hotjar/browser', '@fullstory/browser', '@microsoft/clarity', logrocket, smartlook-client, posthog-js, com.unity.services.analytics, com.unity.analytics, com.google.firebase.analytics, com.gameanalytics.sdk]
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(getAnalytics\s*\(|static\.hotjar\.com|clarity\.ms/tag)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-03
    title: No dark patterns
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No fake urgency or scarcity, confirmshaming, pre-ticked options, nagging after a choice,
      obstruction to leave or cancel, fake notifications, or confusing double negatives.
    rationale: DSA Art. 25, UCPD. The CPC Network's 2026 Joint Statement names misleading countdown timers and false scarcity in games. The DFA proposal blacklists these in all circumstances.
    improvement: Rewrite the copy neutrally, remove timers and pre-selected options, make 'no' as easy as 'yes'.
    effort: low
    sources: [DSA, UCPD, CPC-JS, DFA, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(only \d+ left|offer ends in|hurry[,!]? |last chance|don''t miss out|limited time offer|só restam \d+|última oportunidade|oferta termina|despacha-te|não percas)'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(no thanks,? i (don''t|do not) want|não,? não quero aprender|i prefer to stay (bad|behind))'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(defaultChecked|checked)\s*=\s*\{?\s*true'}

  - id: CORE-COM-04
    title: Purchases are adult-facing only
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Children are never directly exhorted to buy, or to ask adults to buy for them, and any purchase flow
      is behind an adult gate (guardian or school account), with the price in real currency. This applies
      to any product likely to appeal to children, even if it is not aimed at them, and an age gate does
      not remove the duty. Spending real money is off by default, and parental controls work, with
      defaults that suit the age.
    rationale: >
      UCPD Annex I point 28 (direct exhortation to children). KIDS Act Art. 13 and 14(1)(c). CPC Key
      Principle 7: children are always vulnerable, and age gates do not reduce the trader's
      responsibility. The CPC Network's 2026 Joint Statement found games that still urge children to buy.
    improvement: Move purchases to a guardian or school portal; remove buy prompts from child screens.
    effort: medium
    sources: [UCPD, CPC-VC, CPC-JS, KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(UnityPurchasing\.Initialize|IDetailedStoreListener|IStoreListener|CodelessIAPStoreListener)\b'}
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [react-native-iap, expo-in-app-purchases, '@revenuecat/purchases-js', react-native-purchases, cordova-plugin-purchase, in_app_purchase, purchases_flutter, com.unity.purchasing, com.unity.services.purchasing]}
        - {type: manifest, check: monetisation_for_minors, confidence: high}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: safety by design
  - id: CORE-SAF-01
    title: Most protective settings by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Profiles private, sharing off, contact off, notifications off, recommendations of other users
      off by default. The product never relaxes these defaults on its own. Only an adult, or a 16 or 17
      year old after clear information and an explicit choice (AGE-B5-01), can change them.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 8(1) and 11(1). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Flip the defaults in the settings model and add a test that asserts them.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(isPublic|publicProfile|profileVisibility|shareEnabled|allowMessages|discoverable)\s*[:=]\s*(true|[''"]public[''"])'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-02
    title: Notifications only about the child's own activity, off by default, quiet hours
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [notifications]
    requirement: >
      Push notifications are off by default, never designed to prompt the child to start or resume
      use, only relate to the child's own activity or teacher assignments, and respect school time
      and core sleep hours.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(b) and 11(1)(d), applied to games via Art. 15(1).
    improvement: Default the push flag to false, remove re-engagement campaigns, add quiet hours (e.g. 21:00 to 08:00 and school hours).
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(push(Notifications)?Enabled|notificationsEnabled|enablePush)\s*[:=]\s*true'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(we miss you|come back and play|your friends are waiting|it''s been a while|temos saudades|volta a jogar|os teus amigos estão à tua espera)'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-03
    title: Natural stopping points, no autoplay or endless feeds
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No autoplay of the next content and no infinite scroll. Sessions have natural endings and
      regular interruption moments that let the child decide whether to continue.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(a). DFA proposal gives users the right to switch off autoplay.
    improvement: Remove autoplay; end each activity with a clear 'done' screen and an explicit choice to continue.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, DSA-G28, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(autoPlayNext|autoplayNext|autoplay\s*[:=]\s*true|<video[^>]*\sautoplay)'}
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [react-infinite-scroll-component, react-infinite-scroller, ngx-infinite-scroll, vue-infinite-loading]}

  - id: CORE-SAF-04
    title: Time-awareness tools
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product offers break reminders and lets guardians or teachers set a daily time limit,
      protecting school time (outside class use) and core sleep hours.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(3) and 20(4)(a) require time-limited access for social and video services. Best practice for all products.
    improvement: Add a session timer with a gentle break screen and a configurable daily limit.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-COM]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-05
    title: No contact from strangers; play stays in closed groups
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [communication]
    requirement: >
      Nobody outside the child's approved group (class, guardian-approved contacts) can initiate
      contact, see the child's profile or content, or add the child to a group. Multiplayer happens in
      groups set up by a teacher or guardian; play across groups only through pairing arranged by
      adults. The product cannot be used to lure children to other services.
    rationale: >
      DSA Art. 28 and guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(1), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(c) and 15(2).
      Merges A-SOC-01 (retired in 0.11.0).
    improvement: Scope all interaction to closed groups managed by a teacher or guardian (class rooms with join codes); remove user search and contact suggestions; block external links and handles (CORE-CHT-05).
    effort: high
    sources: [DSA, DSA-G28, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(searchUsers|findFriends|suggestedFriends|peopleYouMayKnow|friendSuggestions|addFriendByName|randomMatch|findRandomPlayer|joinPublicRoom|publicLobby|globalChat|worldChat)'}


  - id: CORE-SAF-06
    title: Reports are acknowledged, answered and followed by help
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [communication, ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Wherever children interact with others or with generated content, they can report it, AI output
      included. After a report the child (1) sees at once, in words for their age, that it arrived, what
      happens next and when; (2) gets help information straight away (a trusted adult, the national
      helpline); (3) is told the outcome when it is handled, without details about other children ("we
      took action", or "we looked and did not find a problem, and this is why"); and (4) can say "it is
      still happening", which reopens the report. Reports from minors are handled first.
    rationale: >
      DSA Art. 16(5) requires telling the person who reported about the decision without undue delay. KIDS
      Act Art. 19 asks for child-friendly reporting and support. Children stop reporting when nothing seems
      to happen. The report and block tools themselves are in CORE-CHT-02.
    improvement: Add an acknowledgement screen and an outcome message in child language, a "still happening" button that reopens the case, and a measure of time from report to outcome.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA, DSA-G28, CB-AP]
    detection:
      method: manual


  - id: CORE-SAF-07
    title: Tools for guardians and teachers that respect the child
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Guardians (or teachers in school use) can manage settings, time and contacts. The child is
      told when such tools are active. Controls cannot be bypassed by the child.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 20, applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(d).
    improvement: Provide a guardian or teacher panel for settings, time limits and contacts, with an in-app notice to the child.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-08
    title: Proportionate, privacy-preserving age assurance
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Where age matters, age assurance is proportionate, uses zero-knowledge solutions such as the
      EU age verification app, does not store identity documents and only keeps an age signal.
      Self-declaration alone is not relied on for high-risk features.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 27 and 28: age assurance must be accurate and privacy-preserving, and its data may
      never be used to identify, track, target, advertise to or profile the user (Art. 28(1)). Art. 31
      requires Member States to provide free EU age verification and guardian attestation means.
      DSA Art. 28 guidelines. EU age verification Recommendation.
    improvement: >
      Integrate the EU age verification solution or the EUDI wallet, and the national guardian
      attestation when available (KIDS Act Art. 31); store only an 'over threshold' flag and never
      reuse age assurance data for any other purpose.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, AVREC]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(id_?card_?(image|photo|upload)|passport_?(image|photo|upload)|upload(Id|Passport)Document)'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-09
    title: Children can control and give feedback on what they see
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B3, B4, B5]
    requirement: >
      Children can adjust settings that affect how they interact and what they are shown, give
      feedback with lasting effect, and easily return to default settings.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 18.
    improvement: Add a simple 'my settings' screen with a 'reset to safe settings' button.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-10
    title: No social comparison or image-altering features
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No follower counts, likes on the child's appearance, beauty filters, or features that
      embellish or idealise the child's image.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(3).
    improvement: Remove public counters and appearance filters; use avatars instead of photos.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(followerCount|followersCount|likeCount|beautyFilter|faceFilter|skinSmooth)'}


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: AI
  - id: CORE-AI-01
    title: No emotion recognition on learners
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: The product does not infer emotions of learners from face, voice, posture, typing or other biometric signals.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) prohibits emotion recognition in education institutions since 2 Feb 2025.
    improvement: Remove emotion inference. Use explicit signals (a help button, a self-report mood picker).
    effort: medium
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: high, names: [fer, hume, '@humeai/voice', affdex, '@affectiva/affdex', emotion-recognition, py-feat]}
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(withFaceExpressions|detectEmotion|emotionRecognition|recognizeEmotion|facialExpression|sentimentFromFace|frustrationDetect)'}

  - id: CORE-AI-02
    title: No manipulative AI exploiting age
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      AI features do not use subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques, or exploit age-related
      vulnerability, to change a child's behaviour in a harmful way.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 5(1)(a)(b).
    improvement: Review prompts and reward logic for persuasion targets that serve engagement over learning; document the review.
    effort: medium
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-AI-03
    title: AI interaction and AI-generated content are disclosed
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Children (and teachers) are told, in age-appropriate form, when they interact with AI and
      when content is AI-generated. Generated media is marked.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 50, applicable from 2 Aug 2026.
    improvement: Add a persistent 'AI' label on AI responses and metadata marking on generated images and audio.
    effort: low
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [openai, '@anthropic-ai/sdk', anthropic, '@google/generative-ai', '@google/genai', google-generativeai, '@mistralai/mistralai', mistralai, groq-sdk, ai, '@ai-sdk/openai', langchain, '@langchain/core', elevenlabs, '@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js']}

  - id: CORE-AI-04
    title: AI inventory and no training on learners' data by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative, ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
    requirement: >
      Every AI component is listed (model, provider, purpose, inputs, outputs, oversight). Provider
      data retention for training is disabled. Learners' data is not used to train or fine-tune
      models without a DPIA and a lawful basis.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 5 and 35. AI Act Art. 4 (AI literacy) and provider transparency.
    improvement: Create docs/ai-inventory.md and switch providers to zero-retention or no-training settings.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: ai_without_inventory, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-AI-05
    title: Age-appropriate AI input and output filters
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Input and output filters are set for the target age band and the product's languages, block content
      unsuitable for that age, and fail safe: no answer rather than an unfiltered one. Testing before and
      after release is in CORE-AI-09.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(e)(f) for chatbots and companions. Best practice for any child-facing generative AI.
    improvement: Set filters per age band and language; send filter failures to a safe fallback message.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual


  - id: CORE-AI-06
    title: No AI persona that simulates a relationship
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      AI characters are friendly but never claim feelings, friendship, missing the child, or
      exclusivity, and do not create emotional dependency (see CORE-AI-08 for conversation memory).
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 3(5)(c) and 14(1)(a)(b): such a system would be an 'AI companion' in scope,
      even in an educational product. DFA proposal: right to switch off relationship-simulating chatbots.
    improvement: Rewrite the system prompt persona; add tests that reject outputs claiming feelings or friendship.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, AIA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(i missed you|i love you|i''m your (best )?friend|you are my (best )?friend|only i understand you|don''t leave me|tive saudades tuas|sou o teu melhor amigo|és o meu melhor amigo|não me deixes)'}

  - id: CORE-AI-07
    title: Human review of decisions about learners
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
    requirement: >
      No grade, level placement, certification or access decision about a learner is taken solely
      by automated processing. A teacher can see, explain and override it.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 22. AI Act Annex III(3) human oversight requirements from 2 Dec 2027.
    improvement: Make automated results provisional until a teacher confirms; show the reasons.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: accessibility
  - id: CORE-ACC-01
    title: WCAG 2.2 AA
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Interfaces meet WCAG 2.2 level AA (aligned with EN 301 549), with automated checks in CI
      and manual screen-reader testing per release.
    rationale: European Accessibility Act for covered services; public procurement rules for schools.
    improvement: Add axe-core or Pa11y to CI and fix contrast, labels, focus order and keyboard access.
    effort: medium
    sources: [EAA, WCAG22, EN301549]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.html', '*.jsx', '*.tsx', '*.vue', '*.svelte'], pattern: '<img(?![^>]*\balt=)[^>]*>'}

  - id: CORE-ACC-02
    title: No flashing content
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Nothing flashes more than three times per second.
    rationale: WCAG 2.3.1. Photosensitive seizure risk.
    improvement: Slow or remove flashing effects; offer a 'reduce motion' setting that respects prefers-reduced-motion.
    effort: low
    sources: [WCAG22, EAA, EN301549, W3C-233]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-ACC-03
    title: Inclusive design for children with special educational needs
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Adjustable speed and time limits, audio alternatives for text, captions, dyslexia-friendly
      typography options, and support for switch or keyboard-only play.
    rationale: Accessibility beyond the AA floor is what makes a learning product usable by every child.
    improvement: Add a settings panel for speed, audio, captions and font; test with SEN teachers.
    effort: medium
    sources: [WCAG22, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: security
  - id: CORE-SEC-01
    title: No secrets in the repository
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: API keys, tokens and passwords are not committed.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 32 (security of processing).
    improvement: Rotate the exposed key, move it to a secret manager, and add gitleaks to CI.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}|-----BEGIN (RSA |EC )?PRIVATE KEY-----)'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-02
    title: Access control on every store of learner data
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every table, bucket or collection with learner data enforces access control at the data
      layer (e.g. row-level security), not only in the client.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 25 and 32. Client-only checks are easily bypassed.
    improvement: Enable row-level security with policies scoped to class and role; add a test per table.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.sql'], flags: i, pattern: 'disable row level security'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-03
    title: Encryption in transit
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: All network calls use TLS. No plain http endpoints for APIs or assets.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 32.
    improvement: Switch the URL to https and enable HSTS.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '[''"]http://(?!localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|0\.0\.0\.0|www\.w3\.org|schemas\.|xmlns)[^''"]+[''"]'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-04
    title: No personal data in logs
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Application logs contain pseudonymous IDs only, with short retention.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 32. Logs are often copied to third-party tools.
    improvement: Log the learner ID instead of names or emails; add a log scrubber.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(console\.(log|info|warn|error)|logger\.\w+|print)\s*\([^)]*\b(email|fullName|full_name|firstName|first_name|lastName|phone|password)\b'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-05
    title: Vulnerability handling and breach response
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A published way to report vulnerabilities (SECURITY.md or security.txt), a process to fix them,
      and a breach procedure that lets controllers meet the 72-hour notification deadline.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 33. Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations for products with digital elements.
    improvement: Add SECURITY.md and an incident runbook with contact chain and timelines.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, CRA]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: security_policy_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-SEC-06
    title: Strong authentication for adults, simple safe login for children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Teacher and admin accounts use MFA. Children use age-appropriate login (class code,
      picture password, teacher reset) without email or phone collection.
    rationale: Adult accounts hold data on whole classes. Children should not need personal contact details to log in.
    improvement: Enforce MFA for staff roles; replace child email login with class codes.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: several countries and shared infrastructure
  # Many products are built for several countries at once, and Member States are starting to build shared
  # education infrastructure (EDU-EDIC, 2026). These rules prepare the architecture for both.
  # Guide: framework/05-several-countries.md.
  - id: CORE-INT-01
    title: Country rules are configuration, not code
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Rules that differ between countries live in per-country configuration, not in code: the age of digital
      consent and guardian consent steps, retention periods, national approvals (for example MIME in
      Portugal), safeguarding contacts and helplines, languages, school calendars and curriculum mappings.
      Each value has an owner and a source. An unknown country falls back to the most protective value.
      Adding a country is a configuration change and a review, not a code change.
    rationale: >
      GDPR Art. 8 lets each Member State set the age of digital consent between 13 and 16, and national rules
      on school surveys, safeguarding and retention differ. A product sold in several countries, or offered
      through shared infrastructure such as the EDU-EDIC, needs these differences to be explicit, reviewable
      and testable. Hard-coded values silently apply one country's rules everywhere.
    improvement: Move country-specific values into one versioned file per country, reference it as `country_config` in csef.yaml, and default to the strictest value.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, EDU-EDIC]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: country_config_missing, confidence: medium}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(age_?of_?(digital_?)?consent|digital_?consent_?age|consent_?age|min(imum)?_?consent_?age)["'']?\s*[:=]\s*1[3-6]\b'}

  - id: CORE-INT-02
    title: Schools can take their data and leave
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The school, or whoever buys the product, can export all of its data at class and school level in
      documented, machine-readable open formats: rosters, results, learner-created work and settings, with
      the schema published. Where the product exchanges data with school systems it uses open standards
      (OneRoster for rosters and results, LTI 1.3 for launching from a learning platform). The exit process is
      documented with timelines, and switching costs nothing beyond the subscription.
    rationale: >
      Data Act Chapter VI gives customers of data processing services, SaaS included, a right to switch and
      prohibits switching charges from 12 January 2027 (Art. 29). GDPR Art. 20 covers portability for each
      learner (CORE-DAT-06). Interoperable infrastructure and less lock-in are aims of the EDU-EDIC.
    improvement: Add a school-level export in CSV or JSON with a published schema (OneRoster where it fits), describe the exit process in the contract, and test a full export each release.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DATA-ACT, GDPR, 1EDTECH, EDU-EDIC]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-INT-03
    title: Sign-in and rosters come from the school, with the minimum data
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [accounts]
    requirement: >
      In schools, learners and teachers sign in through the school's identity provider (OpenID Connect or
      SAML) or are launched from the school's learning platform (LTI 1.3), instead of creating separate
      product accounts. Roster imports carry only the fields the product needs (no birth dates, addresses or
      national identity numbers unless a rule requires them), and learner records use pseudonymous
      identifiers.
    rationale: >
      Fewer separate accounts mean fewer stored passwords and less personal data (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 25).
      Standard sign-in and launch let the same product run in several countries and on shared infrastructure
      such as the EDU-EDIC without rebuilding each integration.
    improvement: Support OpenID Connect sign-in and LTI 1.3 launch, trim roster imports to the minimum fields, and key learner records on pseudonymous IDs.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, 1EDTECH, EDU-EDIC]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-INT-04
    title: Critical dependencies are declared and replaceable
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every third party records where it is established (`jurisdiction`) as well as where it hosts data
      (`region`), and whether the product stops working without it (`critical`). A critical provider
      established outside the EU or EEA, AI model providers included, has a documented `fallback`: an
      alternative established in the EU behind the same internal interface, or a reduced mode that keeps
      learning available. Features call AI models through one internal interface, so a school or a country
      can require a different model.
    rationale: >
      Data hosted in the EU may still be reachable under the laws of the provider's home country, and one
      provider changing its terms or leaving can stop a product used by thousands of schools. Reducing
      structural dependencies on third-country providers is an aim of the EDU-EDIC. Builds on CORE-DAT-02
      (processor agreements) and CORE-DAT-03 (transfers).
    improvement: Add `jurisdiction`, `critical` and `fallback` to each third party in csef.yaml, put AI calls behind one internal interface, and test the fallback once a year.
    effort: medium
    sources: [EDU-EDIC, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: third_party_jurisdiction_missing, confidence: medium}
        - {type: manifest, check: critical_dependency_without_fallback, confidence: medium}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: content
  - id: CORE-CNT-01
    title: Asset provenance and licences recorded
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every image, sound, font and AI-generated asset has a recorded source, licence, author and,
      for AI assets, the model used.
    rationale: Copyright compliance and AI Act Art. 50 marking of generated content.
    improvement: Keep an assets/PROVENANCE.csv and check it in CI.
    effort: low
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-CNT-02
    title: Age rating self-assessment
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product has a documented age-appropriateness assessment covering violence, fear, language,
      in-app purchases, contact risks and addictive features (PEGI-style descriptors).
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 16 and 17 foresee harmonised age ratings covering monetisation and contact risks.
    improvement: Run a PEGI-style self-assessment and publish the resulting age and descriptors.
    effort: low
    sources: [PEGI, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ PROFILE A: educational games
  - id: A-ECO-01
    title: No paid randomised rewards (loot boxes)
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No loot boxes, gacha, mystery chests or other variable rewards that can be obtained with
      money or with currency purchasable with money.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans variable reward systems on social and video services. The CPC Network asks all game companies to review loot boxes, above all where children can reach them (Joint Statement, 2026). The DFA proposal would ban paid variable rewards for minors.
    improvement: Replace with fixed, visible rewards earned through learning.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, CPC-JS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(loot_?box|lootbox|gacha|mystery_?(box|chest)|openChest|randomReward|caixa_?mist[eé]rio|ba[uú]_?surpresa)'}

  - id: A-ECO-02
    title: No pay-to-win
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Nothing bought with money gives a gameplay or learning advantage.
    rationale: DFA proposal bans pay-to-win for minors. Fairness in learning.
    improvement: Make all progression earnable through play; keep any paid items cosmetic and adult-purchased.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DFA, UCPD]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(buy(Boost|PowerUp|Hint|Lives|Energy)|purchase(Boost|PowerUp|Hint|Lives|Energy)|comprar(Vidas|Energia|Dica))'}

  - id: A-ECO-03
    title: "Virtual currency: real price, one currency, exact amounts"
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Wherever in-game currency can be bought with money (by adults only, CORE-COM-04): (1) the real-world
      price of every item and every currency amount is shown clearly next to it, also when it is paid with
      currency, without counting discounts, promotions or currency earned in play; (2) there is one
      purchasable currency, and no exchanges between currencies are needed to buy something; (3) players can
      buy the exact amount an item needs, not only bundles that leave unwanted leftovers; and (4) spending it
      is off for children unless a guardian approves. Changes to the currency's value are covered by
      CORE-COM-10.
    rationale: >
      The EU consumer authorities read the UCPD and the Consumer Rights Directive this way in their Key
      Principles on in-game virtual currencies (CPC Network, March 2025, principles 1 to 3), and since
      September 2026 they enforce them in coordinated actions against game companies. Prices hidden behind
      currencies, several currencies and forced bundles make the real cost unclear, above all for children.
      KIDS Act Art. 13(1).
    improvement: Show euro prices next to every item and currency pack; merge purchasable currencies into one; sell exact amounts; add guardian approval for children's spending.
    effort: medium
    sources: [CPC-VC, CPC-JS, UCPD, CRD, KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(buy(Gems|Coins|Diamonds|Crystals)|purchase(Gems|Coins|Diamonds|Crystals)|gemPack|coinPack|comprar(Gemas|Moedas|Diamantes))'}


  - id: A-PLY-01
    title: No penalties for not playing
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No energy systems that only refill by waiting or paying, no pets or worlds that decay or die
      when the child is away, no loss of benefits for missing days.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(d) applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(a).
    improvement: Remove decay and energy timers; let the world wait for the child unchanged.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(energyRefill|staminaRefill|refillTimer|petHunger|decayRate|witherTime|cropsWither|energia_?recarga)'}

  - id: A-PLY-02
    title: Non-shaming failure and feedback
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Errors and failures are presented as part of learning, without ridicule, sad animations directed at the child, or public exposure.
    rationale: Psychological safety supports learning, especially for younger children.
    improvement: Review all failure states with an instructional designer; use encouraging, specific feedback.
    effort: low
    sources: [UNCRC-GC25, ARNAB2014]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-ASM-01
    title: In-game assessment is transparent and separated
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_assessment, assessment]
    requirement: >
      When gameplay is used to assess learning (stealth assessment), learners, teachers and guardians
      are told, assessment data is separated from general telemetry, and it is used only for the stated purpose.
    rationale: GDPR transparency and purpose limitation. AI Act Annex III(3)(b) if AI evaluates learning outcomes.
    improvement: Document what is assessed in the teacher guide and the child privacy notice; store assessment data separately.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ PROFILE B: game-based applications
  - id: B-EVL-01
