    COM: [digital citizenship, netiquette, online respect, empathy online, cidadania digital, etiqueta digital]
    CRE: [creativity, coding, programming, computational thinking, digital creativity, criatividade, programacao, pensamento computacional]
    SAF: [online safety, internet safety, cyber safety, cybersecurity, privacy, digital wellbeing, digital well being, seguranca online, seguranca na internet, ciberseguranca, privacidade, bem estar digital]
    PRB: [problem solving, problem-solving, learning to learn, resolucao de problemas, aprender a aprender]
    AI: [ai literacy, artificial intelligence literacy, understanding of ai, responsible use of ai, literacia em ia, literacia de ia, literacia em inteligencia artificial, uso responsavel da ia]
    ANY: [digital literacy, digital skills, digital competence, 21st century skills, future skills, literacia digital, competencias digitais]
  proof: [proven, evidence based, research based, scientifically, clinically, guaranteed, comprovad, baseado em evidencia, cientificamente, garantid]

targets:

  # ================================================================ INF: information and media
  - id: INF-01
    axis: INF
    title: Find and choose sources
    scope: claimed
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners search with a purpose, compare results and choose sources that fit the question.
    why: Searching and filtering is the first DigComp competence and the base of every other information skill.
    look_for: Tasks where learners search, filter or pick between sources and explain the choice.
    ideas: [A detective quest where clues come from sources of different quality, A search challenge with a budget of queries]
    improvement: Add tasks where learners must search, filter and pick a source, and say why it fits.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["1.1"], UNESCO-MIL: ["locate and access information"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, UNESCO-MIL]
    terms: [[search, searching, keyword, query, filter results, pesquisa, pesquisar, palavra chave, motor de busca], [source, sources, result, results, fonte, fontes, resultado, resultados]]

  - id: INF-02
    axis: INF
    title: Judge credibility by checking across sources
    scope: claimed
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners check who is behind information, compare it with other sources (lateral reading) and decide how far to trust it.
    why: UNESCO's MIL curriculum and its 2026 AI companion guide put source checking and informed trust at the centre.
    look_for: Activities that ask learners to verify a claim elsewhere, trace a source or rate credibility with reasons.
    ideas: [Two-tab challenge that rewards checking a claim on another site before answering, Trust meter with reasons instead of a right answer]
    improvement: Turn at least one task into a verification task with a debrief on why trust went up or down.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["1.2"], UNESCO-MIL: ["critically evaluate information"], UNESCO-AIMIL: ["3.3"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, UNESCO-MIL, UNESCO-AIMIL]
    terms: [[credib, reliab, trustworth, trust, verify, verification, check, checked, checking, fact check, cross check, lateral reading, credivel, fiavel, fiabilidade, confianca, verificar, verificacao, confirmar], [source, sources, claim, claims, information, second source, another source, fonte, fontes, afirmacao, informacao, segunda fonte, outra fonte]]

  - id: INF-03
    axis: INF
    title: Recognise persuasion, advertising and commercial intent
    scope: claimed
    features: [purchases]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners recognise advertising, sponsorship and persuasive design, and can say who benefits.
    why: Children are a protected group under consumer law; recognising commercial intent is part of evaluating information.
    look_for: Activities about ads, influencers, sponsored content or persuasive design, with age-appropriate explanations.
    ideas: [Spot-the-ad level, Learners design an honest and a manipulative version of the same ad and compare]
    improvement: Add a short activity that unpacks one ad or persuasive pattern the learners meet in daily life.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["1.2"], UNESCO-MIL: ["evaluate content of all content providers"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, UNESCO-MIL, UCPD, KIDS]
    terms: [[advert, advertising, ad, ads, sponsor, influencer, persuasi, marketing, publicidade, anuncio, anuncios, patrocin, influenciador, persuas], [recognis, recogniz, spot, identify, understand, explain, reconhecer, identificar, perceber, explicar]]

  - id: INF-04
    axis: INF
    title: Spot mis- and disinformation, including synthetic media
    scope: claimed
    features: [ai_generative, ugc]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners recognise false or manipulated content, including AI-generated images, audio and text, and know how to check provenance.
    why: DigComp 3.0 made mis- and disinformation a priority; AILit and UNESCO link it to AI-generated content.
    look_for: Tasks with manipulated or generated media, provenance checks, or correcting false claims.
    ideas: [Real-or-generated round with explanations of the tells and their limits, Trace-the-origin puzzle]
    improvement: Include generated or manipulated examples and teach a check (source, date, reverse search, provenance label).
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["1.2"], AILIT: ["Create 4"], UNESCO-AIMIL: ["2.5", "3.3"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, AILIT, UNESCO-AIMIL, UNESCO-MIL]
    terms: [[misinformation, disinformation, fake news, false information, manipulated, deepfake, synthetic media, ai generated image, desinformacao, noticias falsas, informacao falsa, manipulad, gerado por ia, imagem gerada]]
    need: 1

  - id: INF-05
    axis: INF
    title: Organise, keep and cite information
    scope: claimed
    age_bands: [B3, B4, B5]
    target: Learners save, organise and reference what they found so others can check it.
    why: Managing information is a DigComp competence and supports honest use of sources.
    look_for: Features or tasks for collecting, organising and citing sources.
    ideas: [Evidence board where clues must carry their source, Citation as a game resource]
    improvement: Let learners keep and cite the sources they used, and reward correct attribution.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["1.3"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3]
    terms: [[cite, citation, reference, bibliography, organise information, organize information, save sources, citar, citacao, referencia, bibliografia, organizar informacao]]
    need: 1

  # ================================================================ COM: communication, citizenship and rights
  - id: COM-01
    axis: COM
    title: Interact respectfully and with empathy
    scope: claimed
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners practise respectful, empathetic communication and understand how tone is read online.
    why: Digital behaviour and interaction are DigComp competences; empathy is a DQ (IEEE 3527.1) area.
    look_for: Scenarios about tone, misunderstandings, kindness or conflict online, with discussion.
    ideas: [Rewrite-the-message challenge, Perspective-switch scenes]
    improvement: Add scenarios where learners choose and discuss how to respond to others online.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["2.1", "2.5"], IEEE3527: ["digital empathy"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, IEEE3527]
    terms: [[respect, empathy, kindness, netiquette, tone, digital behaviour, digital behavior, respeito, empatia, gentileza, netiqueta, comportamento digital], [online, message, messages, comment, chat, mensagem, mensagens, comentario]]

  - id: COM-02
    axis: COM
    title: Collaborate through digital tools
    scope: claimed
    features: [multiplayer]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners plan, share and build together using digital tools, with roles and shared reflection.
    why: Collaboration is a DigComp competence and a recurrent quality marker for game-based learning.
    look_for: Cooperative modes, shared goals, roles, and a debrief of how the group worked.
    ideas: [Cooperative puzzles that need every role, Team retrospectives after a mission]
    improvement: Add a cooperative task with roles and a short reflection on how the team worked.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["2.4"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3]
    terms: [[collaborat, cooperat, teamwork, team work, group work, colabora, coopera, trabalho de equipa, trabalho em grupo]]
    need: 1

  - id: COM-03
    axis: COM
    title: Know and use digital rights; take part as citizens
    scope: claimed
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners know their rights online (privacy, expression, information, protection) and practise civic participation.
    why: UN General Comment 25 and the UNESCO MIL curriculum frame literacy as a matter of rights and participation.
    look_for: Content about children's rights online, freedom of expression, participation or complaints.
    ideas: [Rights cards earned by solving situations, Design a fair rule for an online community]
    improvement: Add content that names children's rights online and how to use them.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["2.3"], UNESCO-MIL: ["human rights and dignity"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, UNCRC-GC25, UNESCO-MIL]
    terms: [[children's rights, childrens rights, digital rights, rights online, citizenship, civic participation, freedom of expression, direitos das criancas, direitos digitais, direitos online, cidadania, participacao civica, liberdade de expressao]]
    need: 1

  - id: COM-04
    axis: COM
    title: Respond to hate, harassment and harmful content
    scope: claimed
    features: [chat, ugc, social]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners recognise hate speech, harassment and harmful content, and know how to respond, report and support others.
    why: The UNESCO MIL curriculum names responding to hate content online as a core competence; BIK+ supports it.
    look_for: Scenarios on cyberbullying or hate speech with bystander options and where to get help.
    ideas: [Upstander choices with consequences, Report-and-support walkthrough]
    improvement: Add a scenario on responding to harassment, including reporting and supporting a peer.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["2.5"], UNESCO-MIL: ["respond to hate and radical content online"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, UNESCO-MIL, BIK]

    improvement: Explain report and block in the moment, add a help-a-friend card next to report for a friend, and show what happens after a report.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["4.1", "4.3"]}
    sources: [KIDS, DSA, BIK, CB-AP]
    builds_on: [CORE-CHT-02, CORE-CHT-11, CORE-SAF-06]
    terms: [[report, block, mute, help button, help a friend, ajudar um amigo, denunciar, reportar, bloquear, silenciar, botao de ajuda], [explain, explained, tutorial, tooltip, what happens, explica, explicad, o que acontece]]

  - id: TRN-07
    axis: TRN
    title: No hidden curriculum
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: The product does not model what literacy teaches against, such as AI that claims to be a friend or to know everything, pressure loops or disguised selling.
    why: Children learn from how products behave, not only from lessons. UNESCO and AILit warn about anthropomorphic AI; the KIDS Act and DFA proposals about manipulative design.
    look_for: Copy, dialogue and mechanics that contradict the learning goals (see the conflict phrases of every target).
    ideas: [Review all character dialogue against AI-02, Review reward loops against SAF-04]
    improvement: Remove or rewrite the copy and mechanics flagged as conflicts, and add a review step for new content.
    refs: {AILIT: ["Engage 2"]}
    sources: [UNESCO-AIAGE, AILIT, KIDS, DFA]
    terms: [[hidden curriculum, content review, copy review, dialogue review, curriculo oculto, revisao de conteudos, revisao de dialogos]]
    need: 1

  - id: TRN-08
    axis: TRN
    title: Personal questions say why they are asked
    scope: feature
    features: [survey]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Before any question about their life, children read or hear why it is asked, who will see the answer and that they can skip it, so answering becomes a lesson in their own data.
    why: GDPR Art. 12 and 13 ask for clear information at the moment data is collected; DigComp 4.2 asks learners to understand how their data is used. A survey is the most concrete data moment a child meets in a product.
    look_for: Child-facing lines before each question or set of questions, a visible skip or "prefer not to say", and a way to see one's own answers later.
    ideas: [Why-we-ask card before the questions, My-answers page the child can open and change]
    improvement: Add one plain sentence per question set on why it is asked and who sees the answer, test it with the age band, and link it in the survey register.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["4.2"]}
    sources: [GDPR, UNCRC-GC25]
    builds_on: [CORE-DAT-13]
    terms: [[why we ask, why are we asking, we ask this, porque perguntamos, para que serve esta pergunta], [skip, prefer not to say, who sees, only you, saltar, prefiro nao dizer, quem ve, so tu]]

  # ================================================================ EDU: educator and family enablement (design lens)
  - id: EDU-01
    axis: EDU
    title: Learning goals stated and mapped to a framework or curriculum
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: The product states what learners will know or be able to do, mapped to DigComp, AILit, the national curriculum or another named framework.
    why: Pedagogical fit and curriculum alignment is the first EU-DEC criterion; learning goals are the starting point of EAF and EdTech for Good reviews.
    look_for: A list of learning goals with framework references (for example DigComp 1.2, AILit Engage 3, Aprendizagens Essenciais).
    ideas: [Goal card per mission, Curriculum map for teachers]
    improvement: Write learning goals per activity and map each to a named framework and age band.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["all"], AILIT: ["all"]}
    sources: [EU-DEC, ET4G2, DIGCOMP3, AILIT]
    terms: [[learning goal, learning goals, learning objective, learning objectives, learning outcome, learning outcomes, objetivo de aprendizagem, objetivos de aprendizagem, aprendizagens essenciais, competencias], [curriculum, framework, digcomp, ailit, aligned, mapped, curriculo, referencial, alinhad, mapead]]

  - id: EDU-02
    axis: EDU
    title: Teacher guidance for before, during and after use
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: >
      Teachers get a guide with set-up, facilitation tips and debrief questions that link play to the literacy
      goals. Where children communicate, the guide has a short part on bullying: how to set open hours, keep
      two children apart, read reports, and use the school's anti-bullying procedure or the product's
      default one.
    why: The EU-DEC guidelines and EdTech for Good stress educator judgement and professionalism; in game-based learning the debrief is where learning is made explicit.
    look_for: Teacher guide, lesson plans, debrief or discussion questions.
    ideas: ["Three-step lesson card: frame, play, debrief", Printable discussion prompts]
    improvement: Add a teacher guide with a debrief for each literacy goal and, for products with communication, a one-page bullying section.
    refs: {}
    sources: [EU-DEC, ET4G2, ARNAB2014]
    terms: [[teacher guide, teachers guide, lesson plan, lesson plans, debrief, discussion questions, facilitat, guia do professor, plano de aula, planos de aula, debriefing, questoes para discussao, orientacoes para professores]]
    need: 1

  - id: EDU-03
    axis: EDU
    title: Evidence of learning beyond engagement
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: The product or its documentation shows how learning of the targets can be seen (formative checks, learner products, evaluation), not only time on task or points.
    why: Impact and assessment is an EU-DEC criterion; EdTech for Good asks for outcome measurement beyond engagement; the Dutch 3E framework grades evidence strength.
    look_for: Assessment aligned to goals, evaluation plans or results, without surveillance of learners and without personal questions beyond a survey register.
    ideas: [Exit-ticket after each mission, Portfolio of learner decisions]
    improvement: Add a light formative check per goal and plan a small evaluation with a partner school, collecting evidence under the CSEF rules on personal questions (CORE-DAT-13 to 18).
    refs: {AILIT: ["learner expectations"]}
    sources: [EU-DEC, ET4G2, NL-3E]
    terms: [[assessment, evaluation, evidence of learning, learning outcomes, formative, exit ticket, pilot, piloted, study, avaliacao, evidencias de aprendizagem, formativa, piloto, estudo]]
    need: 1

  - id: EDU-04
    axis: EDU
    title: Age-appropriate progression
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Literacy targets are sequenced by age band or level (basic, intermediate, advanced), and AI features respect age guidance.
    why: AILit gives learner expectations at three levels; DigComp 3.0 has four proficiency levels; UNESCO asks for context-sensitive, age-appropriate AI.
    look_for: Progression tables, age bands per activity, and age rules for AI features.
    ideas: [Same goal at three levels of challenge, Age gate for independent AI use]
    improvement: Map each goal to an age band and level, and state age rules for AI features.
    refs: {DIGCOMP3: ["proficiency levels"], AILIT: ["learner expectations"]}
    sources: [DIGCOMP3, AILIT, UNESCO-AIAGE]
    terms: [[age band, age group, ages, years old, year olds, faixa etaria, grupo etario, anos de idade], [progression, level, levels, basic, intermediate, advanced, progressao, nivel, niveis, basico, intermedio, avancado]]

  - id: EDU-05
    axis: EDU
    title: Accessible and inclusive literacy learning
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Learners with different needs, languages and backgrounds can reach the same literacy goals.
    why: Design, accessibility and inclusion is an EU-DEC criterion and an EdTech for Good pillar; the European Accessibility Act applies to many services.
    look_for: Accessibility features, language options, alternative paths, and testing with diverse learners.
    ideas: [Read-aloud and dyslexia-friendly mode, "Same mission with visual, audio or text clues"]
    improvement: Offer alternative paths to each goal and test with learners with diverse needs.
    refs: {}
    sources: [EU-DEC, ET4G2, EAA]
    terms: [[accessib, inclusive, inclusion, special educational needs, screen reader, dyslexi, multilingual, acessib, inclusiv, inclusao, necessidades educativas, leitor de ecra, dislexia, multilingue]]
    need: 1

  - id: EDU-06
    axis: EDU
    title: AI literacy support for school staff
    scope: feature
    features: [ai_generative, ai_adaptive, ai_assessment]
    age_bands: [all]
    target: When the product uses AI, the provider gives schools material so staff understand what the AI does, its limits and how to oversee it.
    why: AI Act Art. 4, as recast by the AI Omnibus, asks providers and deployers (often the school) to take measures supporting staff AI literacy; Art. 26 requires competent human oversight for high-risk systems.
    look_for: Staff guides, training, explainers of the AI and its oversight.
    ideas: [Ten-minute staff explainer of the AI, Oversight checklist for teachers]
    improvement: Provide a short staff explainer and oversight guide for every AI feature.
    refs: {}
    sources: [AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS, EU-EDUPKG]
    terms: [[staff, teachers, educators, school, professores, docentes, escola], [ai literacy, training, explainer, human oversight, oversight, literacia em ia, formacao, supervisao]]

  - id: EDU-07
    axis: EDU
    title: Guidance for families
    scope: universal
    age_bands: [all]
    target: Families get short material on what the product teaches, how to talk about it at home and which settings they control.
    why: The KIDS Act proposal requires tools for guardians; the Education Package's Healthy Screens Pledge links schools and families; BIK+ supports parents.
    look_for: Parent or guardian guides, conversation starters, family settings explained.
    ideas: [Talk-about-it card after each unit, Family settings page in plain language]
    improvement: Add a one-page family guide with conversation starters linked to the literacy goals.
    refs: {}
    sources: [KIDS, EU-EDUPKG, BIK]
    terms: [[parent, parents, guardian, guardians, family, families, caregiver, pais, encarregados de educacao, familia, familias, cuidadores]]
    need: 1

# Serious-game quality criteria, mapped to CSEF.
#
# Basis: Caserman et al. (2020), "Quality criteria for serious games: serious part, game part, and balance"
# (source R-CASERMAN2020). The 22 aspects of its three tables are paraphrased here; read the paper for the
# full text. The paper is one of the two publications behind the quality label of the Serious Games
# Gütegemeinschaft. The label's own test rules are not public, so this map is a pre-check, not the label.
#
# Fields
#   id          SG-01 to SG-22
#   group       serious | game | balance
#   aspect      short name of the quality aspect
#   asks        what an assessor looks for (paraphrased)
#   coverage    how much CSEF already checks: covered | partial | declaration | tension
#   rules       CSEF rules whose scan results count for this criterion (only rules in scope count)
#   compass     Compass targets whose document level counts, with the minimum level (2 Designed, 3 Tested)
#   declare     true when the team must add a statement with evidence in csef.yaml (serious_game.claims)
#   evidence    kinds of evidence that fit
#   csef_note   where CSEF is stricter for children; for under-18s the CSEF rule applies

version: "0.1"
basis: R-CASERMAN2020
status: draft

criteria:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ serious part
  - id: SG-01
    group: serious
    aspect: Focus on the characterizing goal
    asks: The learning or training goal stays in focus during play, and game elements do not get in its way.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [A-MOT-03, CORE-DES-02]
    compass: {EDU-01: 2}
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, playtest]

  - id: SG-02
    group: serious
    aspect: Clear goals
    asks: Players always know what to do to move towards the goal; complex games show it first or offer a tutorial.
    coverage: partial
    rules: []
    compass: {EDU-01: 2}
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, playtest]

  - id: SG-03
    group: serious
    aspect: The serious part cannot be skipped
    asks: Learning tasks are needed to play, cannot be avoided, and do not feel like a hurdle before the fun part.
    coverage: declaration
    rules: [A-MOT-01]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, playtest]

  - id: SG-04
    group: serious
    aspect: Correct, neutral content that fits the players
    asks: No subject errors and correct terminology; neutral on political and social issues; suitable for the culture and traditions of the target group.
    coverage: declaration
    rules: [CORE-DES-04]
    compass: {TRN-07: 2}
    declare: true
    evidence: [subject expert review, curriculum mapping]

  - id: SG-05
    group: serious
    aspect: Feedback on progress
    asks: Players see their performance and progress clearly, ideally through more than one sense (visual, audio, haptic).
    coverage: covered
    rules: [A-MOT-02, A-PLY-02, CORE-ACC-05]
    declare: false
    evidence: [screens]

  - id: SG-06
    group: serious
    aspect: Rewards used deliberately
    asks: Positive reinforcement and in-game awards, without rewards that control players and undermine intrinsic motivation.
    coverage: covered
    rules: [A-MOT-01, A-MOT-03, A-MOT-05, C-ENG-03, C-ENG-04, CORE-DES-06]
    declare: false
    evidence: [reward inventory]

  - id: SG-07
    group: serious
    aspect: Proof of effectiveness and lasting effects
    asks: A study shows that players reach the goal and that the effect lasts; randomised controlled trials are the strongest evidence.
    coverage: covered
    rules: []
    compass: {EDU-03: 3}
    declare: false
    evidence: [study]

  - id: SG-08
    group: serious
    aspect: Awards, ratings and expert recommendations
    asks: Game awards, professional and user ratings, expert recommendations, reviews and numbers of players.
    coverage: declaration
    rules: []
    declare: true
    evidence: [award, rating, recommendation, usage figures]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ game part
  - id: SG-09
    group: game
    aspect: Engaging for different player types
    asks: A positive, enjoyable play experience, with something for different kinds of players.
    coverage: declaration
    rules: []
    declare: true
    evidence: [playtest]

  - id: SG-10
    group: game
    aspect: Flow and adaptive difficulty
    asks: Challenge matches skill and grows as players improve ("easy to learn, hard to master"); play is varied; difficulty adapts to the player.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [C-ENG-06, CORE-AI-07]
    compass: {EDU-04: 2, TRN-03: 2}
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, playtest]
    csef_note: Adaptive difficulty that uses learner data must be explained to children (TRN-03); if AI places or evaluates learners, a teacher reviews it (CORE-AI-07).

  - id: SG-11
    group: game
    aspect: Emotional connection
    asks: The game evokes emotions and draws on instincts such as collecting or overcoming danger to keep players engaged.
    coverage: tension
    rules: [CORE-COM-03, CORE-AI-02, CORE-AI-06, C-ENG-04, A-PLY-01]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document]
    csef_note: Emotions yes, pressure no. No guilt, fear of missing out, loss framing, random rewards or AI characters that simulate a relationship.

  - id: SG-12
    group: game
    aspect: Sense of control
    asks: Players control their actions and see how their choices change the game world or the story.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [A-MOT-04]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document]

  - id: SG-13
    group: game
    aspect: Social play and game modes
    asks: Different modes, cooperative and competitive, for players who do better in groups.
    coverage: tension
    rules: [C-ENG-02, CORE-CHT-12, CORE-CHT-02, AGE-B2-01, A-MOT-03]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document]
    csef_note: Competition stays inside the class, with nicknames, a teacher switch and team goals. No public high scores of named children; under 10, preset messages only.

  - id: SG-14
    group: game
    aspect: Immersive experience
    asks: Several senses are engaged (visual, audio, haptic) to create a sense of "being there".
    coverage: partial
    rules: [CORE-DES-01, CORE-DES-03, CORE-ACC-04, CORE-ACC-02]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document]
    csef_note: Under 8, calm screens come first; motion and sound can always be turned down or paused.

  - id: SG-15
    group: game
    aspect: Graphics that fit, and a clear interface
    asks: Graphics suit the purpose, the field and the target group; the interface shows nothing that distracts from the task.
    coverage: covered
    rules: [CORE-DES-03, CORE-DES-05, CORE-ACC-01, CORE-ACC-05]
    declare: false
    evidence: [screens]

  - id: SG-16
    group: game
    aspect: Appropriate sound
    asks: Background music and sound effects suit the game.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [CORE-DES-01, CORE-ACC-04]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ balance
  - id: SG-17
    group: balance
    aspect: Learning built into the gameplay
    asks: Learning tasks are part of the game world and its story, not a gate in front of a reward.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [A-MOT-01]
    compass: {EDU-01: 2}
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, learning and game mechanics map]

  - id: SG-18
    group: balance
    aspect: Scientific foundation and a mixed team
    asks: Game designers and subject experts work together from the start, with the target group, using the state of the art in each field.
    coverage: declaration
    rules: []
    declare: true
    evidence: [team list, co-design record, references]

  - id: SG-19
    group: balance
    aspect: Interaction technology that fits the players
    asks: Devices and controls suit the physical and mental abilities of the target group and the purpose of the game.
    coverage: covered
    rules: [CORE-ACC-01, CORE-ACC-03, AGE-B1-01]
    declare: false
    evidence: [accessibility report]

  - id: SG-20
    group: balance
    aspect: Intuitive controls and tutorials
    asks: Players understand how to play quickly; complex games teach both how to act and what to do.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [CORE-ACC-01]
    declare: true
    evidence: [playtest]

  - id: SG-21
    group: balance
    aspect: No shortcuts around the learning
    asks: Technical features do not let players reach the goal without doing the learning or training, for example by cheating the tracking.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [A-ASM-01, B-EVL-04]
    declare: true
    evidence: [design document, playtest]

  - id: SG-22
    group: balance
    aspect: No adverse effects
    asks: Low risk of accidents, injuries or overload; breaks are suggested; few technical issues and easy maintenance.
    coverage: partial
    rules: [CORE-SAF-03, CORE-ACC-02, CORE-DES-01, C-ENG-06, CORE-SEC-05]
    declare: true
    evidence: [risk notes, maintenance plan]
files.framework/data/profile.yaml:
# CSEF child-safe event profile (csef-ogd-0.1)
# How to log gameplay events for children with the Open Game Data (OGD) event standard
# (Gagnon, Swanson and Harpstead 2024, Table I), and what may travel to each data tier.
# Read with framework/08-learning-data.md. Used by tooling/evidence.py (check-events) and the Workbench.
#
# tiers:   1 event data (controller and its processors), 2 research extracts (named researchers,
#          no key), 3 open evidence (everyone; population features only, see evidence-ontology.yaml)
# verdict: keep | restrict | never
#
# Licence: CC BY 4.0

profile: csef-ogd-0.1
based_on: "Open Game Data event data standard v0.1 (IEEE CoG 2024)"
tiers:
  1: {name: Event data, who: "The controller (the school, or the studio for its own study) and its processors", public: false}
  2: {name: Research extracts, who: "Named researchers under a data sharing agreement, without the key", public: false}
  3: {name: Open evidence, who: "Everyone, CC0. Population features only", public: true}

fields:
  - name: game_id
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2, 3]
    why: "Public fact about the product."

  - name: instance_id
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: "Random per class, group or match. Never a class, school or teacher name."
    why: "A school or class name points to a small group of children."

  - name: player_id
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: >-
      Random, made by the game or the server. Never a hash of an email, name, account or student id.
      One product only. A new code each school year.
    why: "A hash of a known value can be reversed by guessing (EDPB Guidelines 01/2025). Codes shared across products allow profiling."
    rules: [CORE-DAT-20]

  - name: session_id
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: "Random."
    why: "Needed to order and group events."

  - name: timestamp
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1]
    rule: "Tier 1 only. Research extracts use seconds since session start. Open evidence uses the month."
    why: "Exact times plus a school timetable can point to one class."

  - name: offset
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1]
    rule: "Time zone offset only. Dropped in research extracts and open evidence."
    why: "A location hint."

  - name: instance_sequence_index
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2]
    why: "Orders events without exact time."

  - name: session_sequence_index
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2]
    why: "Orders events without exact time."

  - name: event_name
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: "Every event name is declared in the event catalogue, with its purpose."
    rules: [CORE-DAT-19]

  - name: event_source
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: "GAME, or the name of the detector that made the event."

  - name: source_hash
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2, 3]

  - name: event_data
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: >-
      Numbers, booleans and declared values only. No text typed by the child, no voice, drawings,
      chat or names. Every key is declared in the event catalogue.
    why: "Free text is where children write who they are (CORE-DAT-04)."
    rules: [CORE-DAT-04, CORE-DAT-19]

  - name: game_state
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    rule: "Declared keys only (for example unit, score, mode)."

  - name: player_metadata
    verdict: restrict
    tiers: [1, 2]
    allowed_keys: [age_band, captions, text_size, reduced_motion, high_contrast, audio_descriptions, language]
    rule: >-
      Age band (B1 to B5) and the settings in use. Nothing else without a recorded research approval:
      no gender, needs, nationality, language spoken at home or family situation.
    why: "Demographics and needs can reveal special-category data, also indirectly (CJEU, C-184/20)."
    rules: [CORE-DAT-15, CORE-DAT-22]

  - name: game_version
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2, 3]
    rule: "Semantic version. Study builds use a branch name, for example 2.1.0-study."
    rules: [CORE-DAT-25]

  - name: game_log_version
    verdict: keep
    tiers: [1, 2, 3]

# Columns that are not OGD fields and must never appear in an event file.
forbidden_columns:
  - {name: ip, why: "Direct identifier (CORE-DAT-04)."}
  - {name: ip_address, why: "Direct identifier (CORE-DAT-04)."}
  - {name: user_agent, why: "Fingerprinting attribute (CORE-DAT-21, EDPB Guidelines 2/2023)."}
  - {name: email, why: "Direct identifier."}
  - {name: name, why: "Direct identifier."}
  - {name: first_name, why: "Direct identifier."}
  - {name: last_name, why: "Direct identifier."}
  - {name: username, why: "Often a real name."}
  - {name: latitude, why: "Precise location (CORE-DAT-09)."}
  - {name: longitude, why: "Precise location (CORE-DAT-09)."}
  - {name: screen_width, why: "Fingerprinting attribute (CORE-DAT-21)."}
  - {name: screen_height, why: "Fingerprinting attribute (CORE-DAT-21)."}
  - {name: advertising_id, why: "Cross-service tracking id (CORE-DAT-21)."}
  - {name: idfa, why: "Cross-service tracking id (CORE-DAT-21)."}
  - {name: gaid, why: "Cross-service tracking id (CORE-DAT-21)."}
  - {name: school, why: "Points to a small group."}
  - {name: class_name, why: "Points to a small group."}
  - {name: teacher, why: "Identifies an adult and the class."}

# Device facts: one coarse class, sent once per session (for example in session_start event_data).
device_classes: [tablet, laptop, desktop, phone, console, other]

# Signals tooling/evidence.py check-events treats as possible personal data in any value.
value_checks:
  free_text_min_chars: 40          # a string value this long, with spaces, is treated as possible free text
  hash_like: "^[0-9a-f]{32}$|^[0-9a-f]{40}$|^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
files.framework/data/evidence-ontology.yaml:
# csef-evidence-0.1: open evidence features for learning games
# An OGD "ontology": a small set of population features that help teachers choose and plan, published only
# for groups large enough that no child or class can be picked out. Built by tooling/evidence.py build-feed
# from an OGD event file and an event catalogue; checked by evidence.py check-feed, the Workbench and the
# Play to Learn Toolkit. Read with framework/08-learning-data.md.
#
# Licence: CC BY 4.0

ontology: csef-evidence-0.1
profile: csef-ogd-0.1

thresholds:
  min_players: 10          # players behind every published figure
  min_classes: 3           # classes (instance ids) behind every published figure
  round_counts_to: 5       # player and session counts are rounded to this
  time_precision: month    # dates in META.json and README.md

# Event roles an event catalogue can give its events (`evidence_role`). build-feed reads only these.
roles:
  session_start: "A session begins. event_data may carry device (one of the profile's device classes)."
  session_end: "A session ends. event_data.natural_stop (boolean) says if it ended at a natural stopping point."
  unit_start: "A unit (level, mission, chapter) begins. game_state.unit or event_data.unit names it."
  unit_complete: "The unit is finished."
  help: "The player opens a hint or help."
  stuck: "A detector marks the player as stuck in the unit (event_source is the detector, never GAME)."

  - id: EV-STUCK

    toolkit: "Where a teacher should step in (lesson plan tips, Educator Capacity)."
  - id: EV-HELP

    per: unit

    toolkit: "Support needed (Educator Capacity)."
  - id: EV-GAIN

    per: all
    meaning: "Mean change between the pre and post check (score / max), for players with both. The instrument is named in META.json."
    toolkit: "Evidence item V33 for Learning Purpose and Skill Development; lower weight than a peer-reviewed study unless checked."
  - id: EV-ACCESS
    columns_prefix: ev_access_

# CSEF product manifest. Copy to the root of your product repository as csef.yaml.
# It tells the scanner and reviewers what the product is, who uses it and how.
# Keep it honest: undeclared features found in code are reported as such.

cses_version: "0.1"
product: "Product name"
description: "One sentence on what the product does and for whom."

# A = educational game, B = game-based application or software, C = gamified application.
# A product can declare more than one (see framework/00-introduction.md, section 3).
profiles: [A]

# B1 3-5, B2 6-9, B3 10-12, B4 13-15, B5 16-17. List every band that uses the product.
age_bands: [B2, B3]

# 1 = Legal baseline: binding law only.
# 2 = Forward-compliant: plus adopted proposals and official benchmarks (EU KIDS Act, DFA, DSA guidelines).
# 3 = Best practice: plus research and expert recommendations.
compliance_level: 2

# Loads packs/<code>.yaml for each country (EU is the base and needs no pack).
jurisdictions: [EU, PT]

# Required when `jurisdictions` lists two or more countries (CORE-INT-01): one versioned file with the values
# that differ by country (age of digital consent, retention, approvals, helplines, languages, calendars).
# country_config: config/countries.yaml

# Extra packs: national guidance, procurement rules, literature, your own company red lines.
packs: []
#  - .cses/packs/my-company.yaml

context: school               # school | home | mixed
distribution:
  - channel: school           # school | app_store | web | platform
    operated_by: school       # school (or on its behalf) | provider

legal_scope:
  # exempt_educational | in_scope_online_game | in_scope_ai_companion | in_scope_platform | not_applicable | unknown
  kids_act: exempt_educational
  dsa_online_platform: false

gdpr_role: processor          # controller | processor | joint

# Declare every feature present. Rules that depend on a feature only appear when it is declared.
# accounts, multiplayer, chat, ugc, social, notifications, streaks, leaderboards, purchases,
# assessment, ai_generative, ai_assessment, ai_adaptive, recommender, survey
# communication = shorthand for chat, multiplayer, social and ugc together.
# survey = questions to the child or family about the child's life, family, opinions, interests or feelings
# (surveys, "about me" profiles, mood check-ins, onboarding questions). Quizzes about learning are assessment.
features: [accounts]

# Required when `survey` is declared (rules CORE-DAT-13 to 18, CORE-CHT-08).
# survey:
#   register: docs/survey-register.md   # from templates/survey-register.md: each question, purpose, answers, who sees, retention
#   answered_by: guardian               # guardian | child_with_guardian | child  (below 10: guardian or child_with_guardian)
#   teacher_view: aggregate             # aggregate | individual | none
#   min_group: 5                        # smallest group behind any total a teacher sees (5 or more)
#   free_text: false                    # true only with a safeguarding route
#   safeguarding: docs/safeguarding.md  # disclosure route agreed with schools (required if free_text: true)
#   uses: [personalisation]             # personalisation | teacher | evaluation | research
#   research_approval: null             # ethics and national approval record (required for evaluation or research)

# Required when children can communicate (chat, multiplayer, social or ugc). Rules CORE-CHT-14 and CORE-CHT-15.
# moderation:
#   by: teacher                         # teacher | provider | both: who handles reports
#   open_hours: "school days 08:00-18:00, set by the teacher"
#   out_of_hours: closed                # closed | preset_only | provider_moderators
#   languages: [pt, en]
#   response_targets: {urgent: "1 hour", other: "1 school day"}
#   bullying_procedure: school          # school (the school's anti-bullying plan) | templates/bullying-procedure.md (default)

ai:
  inventory: null             # e.g. docs/ai-inventory.md (required if any ai_* feature)
  act_class: none             # none | limited_risk_art50 | high_risk_annex_iii
  risk_file: null             # e.g. docs/ai-risk-file.md (required for ai_assessment / ai_adaptive)

monetisation: none            # none | adult_licence | subscription_adult | in_app_purchases | ads | virtual_currency

third_parties:
  - name: "Hosting provider"
    purpose: "hosting and database"
    region: "eu-central-1"
    jurisdiction: "DE"                 # where the provider is established (CORE-INT-04)
    critical: true                     # the product stops working without it
    # fallback: "second EU provider, restore from backup within 24 h"   # required if critical and established outside the EU/EEA
    dpa_signed: true
    # transfer_mechanism: "SCCs + TIA"   # required if region is outside the EEA

retention:
  - category: "gameplay events"
    period: "end of school year + 30 days"
    enforced_by: "jobs/purge-gameplay.ts"

dpia: docs/dpia.md
security_policy: SECURITY.md

# Literacy Compass (tooling/compass.py): what the product claims to teach.
# Axes: INF information and media, COM communication and rights, CRE creation, SAF safety and wellbeing,
# PRB problem solving, AI AI literacy. Or list target ids (see framework/compass/catalogue.md).
compass:
  claims: []
#  not_applicable:
#    - target: INF-05
#      reason: "Covered elsewhere in the school programme"

# Product description for labels and catalogues (tooling/metadata.py). Exports the Serious Games Metadata Format
# (SG-MDF, DIN SPEC 91380) as JSON and XML, and schema.org LearningResource (JSON-LD) for any learning product.
# Title, summary, age groups, game mode, purchases and the data statement come from the rest of this file.
# Values for the selection lists: DIN SPEC 91380 Annex A (free download, https://doi.org/10.31030/2853739).
# metadata:
#   game_id: my-product                  # stable id; default: slug of the product name
#   primary_goal: Educational Game        # default for profile A
#   goal_descriptions:                    # subject, adverb, verb
#     - {subject: knowledge of player, adverb: sustainably, verb: improve}
#   keywords: [fractions, primary maths]
#   genre: [logic and puzzle games]
#   game_mode: [single player]           # default when no multiplayer feature is declared
#   previews:
#     - {url: "https://...", type: title image}
#   play_time: "15 to 20 minutes per lesson"
#   release: {version: "1.0.0", date: 2026-09-01, status: complete}
#   age_rating: PEGI-3
#   languages: [pt, en]                  # ISO 639
#   privacy_notice: "https://..."
#   distribution:
#     - {channel: school licence, url: "https://...", price_info: "Yearly licence per class", with_costs: "yes"}
#   platforms:
#     - {platform: web browser, requirements: "Current browsers on tablet or laptop"}
#   parties:
#     - {name: My Studio, role: developer, url: "https://..."}
#   quality:                             # awards, ratings, studies (also SG-08 in the pre-check)
#     - {aspect: "Award name, year", type: awards, url: "https://..."}
#   learning:                            # learning-games profile (Level 3)
#     resource_type: [exercise]
#     context: [school]
#     teaching_concept: "Guided discovery, then practice"
#     curriculum: "Curriculum or competence framework it maps to"
#     prior_knowledge: "What players must know before"

# Serious-game pre-check (tooling/precheck.py). Statements with evidence for criteria CSEF cannot read from code.
# Ids SG-01 to SG-22: framework/serious-games/criteria.yaml. Evidence: paths in this repo or links.
# serious_game:
#   characterizing_goal: "Pupils aged 6 to 9 understand and compare simple fractions."
#   claims:
#     SG-03: {statement: "Paths open only when a task is solved.", evidence: [docs/design-document.md]}

# Accepted gaps. A waiver needs a reason, a named approver and an expiry date.
waivers: []
#  - rule: CORE-SEC-03
#    path: "src/legacy/*"
#    reason: "Legacy CDN only serves public images over http; migration ticket #123"
#    approved_by: "DPO, Jane Doe"
#    expires: 2027-03-31

last_review: 2026-11-11
files.templates/event-catalogue.yaml:
# CSEF event catalogue. Copy to your product repository (for example docs/event-catalogue.yaml) and link it
# from csef.yaml under data_collection.event_catalogue.
#
# Every event the product logs, with its fields and its purpose. Nothing that is not here may be logged
# (CORE-DAT-19). tooling/evidence.py check-events compares an event file with this catalogue, and the scanner
# compares event names in code with it.
#
# purpose:       operation | improvement | evaluation | research
#                (research events are logged only in a study build: CORE-DAT-25)
# evidence_role: optional. Lets evidence.py build-feed compute the open evidence features
#                (see framework/data/evidence-ontology.yaml for the roles).
# fields:        event_data keys. type: integer | number | boolean | enum | id. Never free text.

catalogue: csef-event-catalogue-0.1
game_id: my-game
log_version: 1
event_standard: ogd-0.1

events:
  - name: session_start
    purpose: operation
    evidence_role: session_start
    fields:
      device: {type: enum, values: [tablet, laptop, desktop, phone, other]}

  - name: unit_start
    purpose: improvement
    evidence_role: unit_start
    fields:
      unit: {type: id}

  - name: unit_complete
    purpose: improvement
    evidence_role: unit_complete
    fields:
      unit: {type: id}
      attempts: {type: integer}

  - name: hint_used
    purpose: improvement
    evidence_role: help
    fields:
      unit: {type: id}

  - name: setting_changed
    purpose: operation
    evidence_role: setting
    fields:
      setting: {type: enum, values: [captions, text_size, reduced_motion, high_contrast]}
      "on": {type: boolean}

  - name: mode_set
    purpose: operation
    evidence_role: mode
    fields:
      mode: {type: enum, values: [solo, team, teacher_led]}

  - name: check_score
    purpose: evaluation
    evidence_role: assessment
    fields:
      phase: {type: enum, values: [pre, post]}
      score: {type: integer}
      max: {type: integer}

  - name: session_end
    purpose: operation
    evidence_role: session_end
    fields:
      natural_stop: {type: boolean}

# Events made by detectors (event_source is the detector name, never GAME).
detectors:
  - name: stuck
    source: StuckDetector
    purpose: improvement
    evidence_role: stuck
    level: population          # population | teacher_view (teacher_view needs the assessment rules)
    meaning: "Three failed attempts and a help request in the same unit within five minutes."
    fields:
      unit: {type: id}

# Keys allowed in game_state and player_metadata.
game_state: [unit, score, mode]
player_metadata: [age_band, captions, text_size, reduced_motion]

# CSEF source pack template.
#
# A pack extends the framework without forking it. Use it for:
#   - national laws and guidance (a country pack, e.g. packs/es.yaml)
#   - sector or procurement requirements (e.g. a Ministry's rules for digital resources)
#   - research and literature you want cited in reports
#   - your own company red lines (keep company packs in your product repo, e.g. .cses/packs/acme.yaml)
#
# How it is loaded:
#   - packs/<code>.yaml is loaded automatically when the manifest lists `jurisdictions: [<CODE>]`
#   - any other pack is loaded through `packs: [path/to/pack.yaml]` in the manifest,
#     or with `--pack path` on the command line
#
# Merge rules (enforced by the scanner):
#   - sources: added to the registry. An id may not clash with an existing one.
#   - rules: new rules. Use your pack id as prefix (e.g. ES-DAT-01). Same fields as framework/rules.yaml.
#   - amend: change an existing rule, only in the stricter direction:
#       add_sources   cite more sources on the rule
#       note          shown under the rule in reports (national nuance)
#       level         only SHOULD -> MUST
#       tier          only to a lower number (e.g. 2 -> 1 when your country already made it law)
#       add_patterns  extra detection patterns (e.g. local-language UI strings)
#   - parameters: free key/values shown in the report (e.g. digital consent age)
# A pack can never weaken or remove a rule. Waivers are the only way to accept a gap,
# and they need a named approver in the product manifest.

pack:
  id: xx                      # lowercase; also the prefix for new rule ids (XX-...)
  title: "Country or organisation pack"
  jurisdiction: XX            # ISO country code, or 'ORG' for an organisation pack
  version: "0.1.0"
  maintainer: "name or team"
  status: "Draft"

parameters:
  digital_consent_age: 16     # GDPR Art. 8 national choice (13 to 16)

sources:
  - id: XX-LAW-1
    title: "National law title"
    type: law                 # law | law-pending | proposal | guidance | standard | literature | news
    jurisdiction: XX
    status: "In force since ..."
    url: "https://..."
    verified: 2026-01-01

amend:
  - rule: AGE-B4-01
    add_sources: [XX-LAW-1]
    note: "Age of digital consent here is 16."

rules:
  - id: XX-EDU-01
    title: "Short title"
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: "What the product must do."
    rationale: "Why, in one or two sentences."
    improvement: "What a team should change to meet it."
    effort: low
    sources: [XX-LAW-1]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: PT-SUP-01
    title: Help screens point to Portuguese support services
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [multiplayer, chat, ugc, social, ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Support information after a report includes Portuguese resources (Linha Internet Segura)
      and explains in simple words how to get help from a trusted adult.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 19(4) requires informing minors of national support organisations.
    improvement: Add the Linha Internet Segura number and link to the help screen.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, PT-ISEGURA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: PT-SUR-01
    title: Questionnaires to pupils in public schools go through MIME approval (EduQA, I.P.)
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [survey]
    requirement: >
      Questionnaires or surveys applied to pupils in Portuguese public schools for evaluation,
      research or product studies, on paper or inside the product, are submitted to EduQA, I.P. (which took over the DGE's functions) through
      MIME (Monitorização de Inquéritos em Meio Escolar) before use, unless they are registered in the
      national statistical system. The school also authorises, and guardian authorisation is obtained
      where EduQA requires it. Questions that are part of the learning activity itself are agreed
      with the school and kept in the survey register.
    rationale: >
      Despacho 15847/2007 requires prior authorisation for questionnaires and surveys in public
      schools, proposed by internal or external entities, and lets the appraising body (the DGE, now EduQA, I.P.) decide when guardian
      authorisation is needed. Questionnaires with sensitive questions have been withdrawn from schools
      for lacking it.
    improvement: Register evaluation and research questionnaires in MIME, keep the approval number in `survey.research_approval`, and plan the timeline around it.
    effort: medium
    sources: [PT-MIME]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: survey_research_without_approval, confidence: medium}
